regulator: New Mexico Regulation and Licensing Department, Cannabis Control Division

data_source.name: Cannabis Reporting Online Portal (CROP): Sales
data_source.notes: Monthly adult-use ('rec') and medical sales self-reported by licensees through the state's seed-to-sale tracking system, as published on the RLD's CROP portal. Read Nov 7, 2026; the latest month shown was August 2026. Annual figures are sums of the monthly figures.

annual.basis: sum of the official monthly figures
sum of the official monthly figures

tax_note: Adult-use cannabis pays a cannabis excise tax that was 12% until June 2025 and rises one point each July 1 (14% from July 1, 2026) until it reaches 18% in 2030, plus gross receipts tax; medical sales are exempt from the excise tax (NM Taxation and Revenue Department).
summary: New Mexico's adult-use market opened in April 2022 and has settled at roughly $45 million to $50 million a month in combined sales. Licensees reported $47.4 million in August 2026, including $37.3 million adult-use. Combined sales were $590.3 million in 2024 and $567.4 million in 2025. Stores in border towns such as Sunland Park, Clovis and Hobbs draw heavily from Texas, where retail sales are not legal. A very large number of licensed retailers and falling prices keep revenue flat, and the excise tax is stepping up one point each year.

faq.q: How much cannabis does New Mexico sell a month?
faq.a: New Mexico licensees reported $47.4 million in cannabis sales in August 2026: $37.3 million adult-use and $10.1 million medical, per the RLD's CROP portal.

faq.q: How much cannabis did New Mexico sell in 2025?
faq.a: About $567.4 million, of which $435.3 million was adult-use, based on the state's monthly figures.

faq.q: What is New Mexico's cannabis tax rate?
faq.a: The cannabis excise tax is 14% from July 1, 2026, rising one point a year to 18% in 2030, plus gross receipts tax. Medical purchases are exempt from the excise tax.
